headline: SECOND-BEST EVER: Power Metallic Drills 22m @ 11.46% CuEq at Lion Zone, Q3 Resource Estimate on Track
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) reported its second-best-ever intersection at the Lion Zone today: hole 26-095 returned 22.00m grading 11.46% CuEq at its Nisk polymetallic project in Quebec. The company continues building toward a maiden Mineral Resource Estimate expected in Q3 2026.

headline: GOLD REBOUNDS to $4,570 as Trump Pauses 'Project Freedom,' Iran Deal Talks Progress
snippet: Gold climbed back toward $4,570/oz after the White House paused its Strait of Hormuz ship-rescue operation — dubbed 'Project Freedom' — as Washington finalises a deal with Tehran. Oil pulled back from $114/bbl highs, easing the safe-haven headwinds that had dragged gold to a one-month low near $4,540 on Monday.

headline: NEVADA BONANZA: Scorpio Gold Hits 10.40 g/t Over 5.67m Including 455.52 g/t Au at Manhattan District
snippet: Scorpio Gold (TSX-V: SGN) released step-out drill results at its Manhattan District Project in Nevada with hole 26MN-067 returning 10.40 g/t gold over 5.67m — including a bonanza-grade 455.52 g/t over 0.49m — along the Zanzibar Trend. Phase Two drilling has now completed 21,939m across 76 holes, with 18 holes still pending assay.

headline: G2 REACHES 1KM DEPTH: 84.5m @ 3.0 g/t Au Extends OKO Deposit Into Undrilled Ground in Guyana
snippet: G2 Goldfields' deepest-ever drill hole returned 84.5m grading 3.0 g/t gold from 915m at its Oko-Ghanie deposit in Guyana, pushing vertical mineralization to 1 kilometre and extending it 140m into fresh ground. The result adds scale to the deposit ahead of G Mining Ventures' pending acquisition of G2, announced April 9.

headline: URANIUM AT $86.55/lb — AI Data Centers Rewrite Nuclear Demand Models as Supply Gap Widens
snippet: Spot uranium sits at $86.55/lb — up 1.64% month-over-month but below January's $101 peak — as the American Nuclear Society flags a structural supply shortfall: global production of roughly 140 million pounds per year falls short of consumption, with no major new capacity expected for 5–7 years. More than 85% of investors surveyed expect prices to continue rising toward $100–$120/lb.

headline: GOLDMAN TURNS BEARISH on Copper: Cuts Target to $12,650/t, Forecasts 490,000-Tonne Surplus
snippet: Goldman Sachs trimmed its 2026 copper base-case to $12,650/t and now forecasts a 490,000-tonne surplus — up from 380,000 tonnes prior — warning that a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure threatens both sulphuric acid supply chains and global demand. Copper has erased all its 2026 gains since hitting a record $14,500/t in January, and Goldman says fundamentals don't support current prices.

headline: $2.8 Billion Serra Verde Deal: Will USA Rare Earth ACTUALLY Break China's Rare Earth Monopoly?
snippet: The Diplomat offers a sobering analysis of USA Rare Earth's $2.8B Serra Verde acquisition: while a 15-year government-backed offtake secures supply of heavy rare earths Nd, Pr, Tb, and Dy, China produced 16,001 tonnes of rare earth magnets in Q1 2026 alone versus USA Rare Earth's 1,200-tonne target by 2027. Strategic signalling, but limited near-term market impact.

headline: GOLD SWOT: Trident Resources Logs Best-Ever Contact Lake Drill as Mining Equities Show Resilience
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT highlights Trident Resources' strongest-ever drill result at the Contact Lake gold project and examines whether gold mining equities can sustain technical support as the gold price attempts to recover from its 20% correction off January's $5,600/oz peak. The piece weighs the bullish exploration pipeline against the lingering valuation discount of miners to metal.

headline: EXPLORATION RACE: Junior Miners Surge Into High-Grade Discovery Mode After Gold's $5,600 Peak
snippet: African Mining examines which junior miners are winning the post-peak exploration race after gold's Q1 high near $5,600/oz, now corrected ~20%. The piece spotlights drill momentum, commodity diversification, and jurisdiction quality as the key differentiators between juniors that re-rate and those that stall waiting for the next macro catalyst.

headline: SILVER IMPORT RECORD: China Buys 836 Tonnes in March as Sixth Consecutive Deficit Year Confirmed
snippet: GoldSeek's Gold SWOT reports China silver imports hit an all-time monthly high of 836 tonnes in March 2026, driven by solar manufacturing capacity and retail investment demand. The Silver Institute has confirmed a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, with the structural demand gap showing no sign of closing as silver trades at $73.96/oz — up more than 150% year-over-year.
